basic_info: Anna, late twenties, right ankle pain following fall on ice last night
present_illness: Injured right ankle after falling on ice last night; heard a pop at the time of injury; current pain with some ability to bear weight. The pain is on the outside of the ankle, near the bone, and it's a throbbing pain that's constant. It was worse right after the fall but is now around a 6/10. There's some bruising and swelling, especially on the lateral side, and it feels a little warm to the touch. The patient reports that the ankle feels a bit wobbly when moving but denies deformity, instability, numbness, tingling, or weakness. She can bear partial weight but limps slightly. The patient has not experienced any previous sprains of this particular ankle but has a history of soccer-related injuries in high school. She iced the ankle last night and took ibuprofen, but it did not provide significant relief. The patient denies locking, catching, or clicking sensations when moving the ankle.
past_history: No prior injury to this ankle, history of soccer-related injuries in high school
physical_exam: Vital signs: BP 120/80 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, Temp 36.8°C. Physical examination of the right ankle reveals tenderness along the lateral aspect, particularly near the fibula. There is mild swelling and bruising, with warmth to touch. No deformity or gross instability is noted. Range of motion is limited due to pain. No neurological deficits (numbness, tingling, or weakness) are present. The patient can bear partial weight but limps slightly.
aux_exam: X-ray of the right ankle was performed and showed no fractures or bony abnormalities.
